title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Applied Chemistry — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Describe the Haber process for ammonia manufacture. Why is high pressure used?
questions.solution:
N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ + heat. Conditions: 450–500°C (rate vs yield compromise), **~200 atm**, Fe catalyst with Mo promoter, unreacted gases recycled.

**High pressure** because 4 gas moles → 2: Le Chatelier drives the equilibrium toward NH₃, and pressure also speeds collisions.
questions.knowledgeNote: Ammonia feeds fertilisers (urea, ammonium nitrate), explosives, and plastics — the highest-volume synthesis on Earth.

questions.question: What is the Contact process? Write the key reactions and conditions.
questions.solution:
Manufacture of **sulphuric acid**: (1) S + O₂ → SO₂; (2) 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅, 450°C, 1–2 atm); (3) SO₃ + H₂SO₄ → H₂S₂O₇ (oleum); (4) H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄.

SO₃ is absorbed in acid, never water directly (which makes unabsorbable mist).
questions.knowledgeNote: 'King of chemicals' — national H₂SO₄ output tracks industrial capacity, an NEB essay staple.

questions.question: Describe the Ostwald process for nitric acid manufacture.
questions.solution:
(1) Catalytic oxidation: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O (Pt–Rh gauze, ~800°C). (2) 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂. (3) 3NO₂ + H₂O → 2HNO₃ + NO (absorption tower, NO recycled).

Product: ~68% acid, concentrated by distillation.
questions.knowledgeNote: Ostwald links Haber (NH₃) to fertilisers and explosives — the nitrogen-industry chain question.

questions.question: Describe the Solvay process for sodium carbonate manufacture with reactions.
questions.solution:
Brine + ammonia + CO₂: NaCl + NH₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → NaHCO₃↓ + NH₄Cl; then 2NaHCO₃ →(heat) Na₂CO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O.

Ammonia is regenerated from NH₄Cl with lime, and CO₂ from limestone calcination — only limestone and brine are consumed.
questions.knowledgeNote: Fails for K₂CO₃ (KHCO₃ too soluble to precipitate) — the built-in limitation question.

questions.question: What are NPK fertilisers? Why is urea the most widely used nitrogenous fertiliser?
questions.solution:
**NPK** fertilisers supply nitrogen (leaf growth), phosphorus (roots/flowers), potassium (disease resistance).

**Urea** (46.7% N, highest of all) is cheap, highly soluble, non-explosive, and leaves only CO₂ — dominating Nepal's Terai paddy cultivation.
questions.knowledgeNote: Excess N runs off into rivers (eutrophication) — the environmental counterpoint NEB pairs with this question.

questions.question: How is cement manufactured? What happens during the setting of cement?
questions.solution:
Limestone + clay are burnt at ~1500°C to clinker (calcium silicates/aluminates), then ground with ~3% gypsum.

**Setting:** hydration of silicates forms interlocking C–S–H gel crystals; gypsum regulates the flash set of aluminates. Final hardening takes days as the gel densifies.
questions.knowledgeNote: Gypsum retards, never accelerates — its absence would flash-set cement unusably fast.
